Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

disease_intelligence.suggested_geographic_granularity: ["national (United States)", "HHS region", "state", "territory (Puerto Rico, Guam, USVI, etc.)", "county/local (where available)"]
disease_intelligence.suggested_time_granularity: weekly (CDC epidemiological week; target week 40, ending 2024-10-05)
count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences
suggested_query_templates: influenza surveillance report United States [week] October 2024
influenza-associated hospitalizations United States week ending [date] 2024
warnings: task_input_warnings carried forward: source_discovery_not_yet_disease_generic; extraction_record_model_still_hantavirus_named — verify extraction schema is mapped to influenza fields before collection
The target time window (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) corresponds to CDC Epidemiological Week 40 (EW40) of the 2024-2025 influenza season — use EW40 as a primary query anchor
Early-season influenza activity in the US is typically low in EW40; data may be sparse or show 'minimal/sporadic' activity levels rather than discrete case counts

CDC FluView for EW40 2024 would typically be published approximately one week after the week ends (around 2024-10-11) — there may be a reporting lag affecting data availability within the stated window
Avian influenza (H5N1) human cases in the US were being reported in 2024 — strictly exclude these from seasonal influenza collection; they require a separate disease profile
Do not conflate influenza vaccination coverage reports with case/outbreak data
Some state health departments may not publish weekly influenza reports until flu season is declared active — data gaps at state level are expected for this early-season window
Evidence quotes must capture numeric values, geographic scope, time period, and case classification type to be auditable

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

influenza-associated hospitalizations United States week ending [date] 2024

Early-season influenza activity in the US is typically low in EW40; data may be sparse or show 'minimal/sporadic' activity levels rather than discrete case counts

Avian influenza (H5N1) human cases in the US were being reported in 2024 — strictly exclude these from seasonal influenza collection; they require a separate disease profile
Do not conflate influenza vaccination coverage reports with case/outbreak data
Some state health departments may not publish weekly influenza reports until flu season is declared active — data gaps at state level are expected for this early-season window
Evidence quotes must capture numeric values, geographic scope, time period, and case classification type to be auditable

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

Do not conflate influenza vaccination coverage reports with case/outbreak data
Some state health departments may not publish weekly influenza reports until flu season is declared active — data gaps at state level are expected for this early-season window
Evidence quotes must capture numeric values, geographic scope, time period, and case classification type to be auditable

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Influenza (Seasonal) from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Influenza (Seasonal) from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.

count_semantics_notes: CDC FluView reports influenza activity by geographic spread level (sporadic, local, regional, widespread) — these are NOT raw case counts
ILINet reports % of outpatient visits for ILI — this is a rate/proportion, not a case count
FluSurv-NET reports hospitalization rates per 100,000 population — convert to counts only if population denominators are available
Laboratory-confirmed case counts may be underreported due to testing rates; treat as minimum estimates
Pediatric influenza deaths are individually reported to CDC; adult deaths are modeled estimates
Cumulative vs. weekly counts must be clearly distinguished in extraction
State-level case counts may differ from CDC aggregate due to reporting lag
disambiguation_risks: 'Flu' may colloquially refer to gastroenteritis ('stomach flu') — exclude non-respiratory flu references
Avian influenza (H5N1, H5N2) human spillover cases must be tracked separately from seasonal influenza
Influenza A vs. Influenza B subtype distinctions may affect case classification
ILI (influenza-like illness) counts are syndromic and not confirmed — distinguish from laboratory-confirmed case counts
Pandemic influenza (e.g., 2009 H1N1) terminology may appear in historical context — scope to seasonal 2024-2025
CDC FluView reports activity levels (minimal/low/moderate/high/very high) rather than raw case counts — note semantic difference
Hospitalization rates (per 100,000) vs. raw hospitalization counts — clarify units during extraction
Pediatric influenza mortality is nationally notifiable; adult mortality is estimated — note data source differences

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Influenza (Seasonal).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluView Interactive and CDC Influenza Division weekly surveillance reports covering MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) for the United States, including ILI activity, laboratory-confirmed influenza counts, hospitalizations, and deaths.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC FluView is the primary authoritative weekly influenza surveillance report for the United States and is the highest-priority collection source for this task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FluSurv-NET (Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network) data for MMWR Week 40 2024 covering laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in the United States.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FluSurv-NET provides hospitalization rates and counts for laboratory-confirmed influenza, directly supporting the hospitalizations target field.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state-level health department influenza surveillance reports or weekly flu updates published during or covering the period 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05 for U.S. states and territories.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments publish subnational influenza data that can populate subnational_location and locality fields not available in national aggregates.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC WONDER or HHS Protect public data portal datasets containing influenza case, death, or hospitalization records for the United States for the target time window.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Structured databases from CDC and HHS may provide machine-readable records with precise date and count fields.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify WHO FluNet or PAHO influenza surveillance reports covering the United States for MMWR Week 40 2024 to serve as an independent validation source.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: WHO FluNet aggregates national influenza laboratory data independently from CDC FluView and can validate case counts and subtype distributions.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify HealthMap, ProMED, or GOARN situation reports referencing influenza activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Independent surveillance aggregators provide secondary validation signals for outbreak detection and case counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions and ILI surveillance methodology documents for the 2024-2025 influenza season to support correct interpretation of count semantics.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Understanding whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or ILI-based is essential for correct field mapping and evidence quote interpretation.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature or preprints describing early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States to provide case definition and baseline context.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Literature sources help interpret surveillance data and provide case definitions for confirmed vs. suspected counts.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag any sources that aggregate influenza data across multiple weeks or seasons without week-specific breakdowns, or that conflate seasonal influenza with avian influenza (H5N1/H5N2), for human review.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Aggregated or conflated sources risk introducing out-of-window counts or excluded disease terms into the collection.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC FluView, CDC FluSurv-NET, CDC WONDER, HHS Protect, and U.S. state/territory health department weekly influenza surveillance reports are the primary authoritative sources for influenza case, death, and hospitalization data in the United States. MMWR Week 40 (2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05) reports are the direct target. Key agencies: CDC Influenza Division (cdc.gov/flu), all 50 state health departments, D.C. and U.S. territories.

WHO FluNet provides country-level laboratory-confirmed influenza specimen data for the United States, independently aggregated from national surveillance. PAHO regional influenza updates may also cover the U.S. for the target week. These serve as independent validation against CDC FluView collection records.

CDC FluView Interactive (online dashboard), HHS Protect public data, and HealthData.gov influenza datasets provide machine-readable structured records that can be queried for MMWR Week 40 2024 data. These support both collection and validation roles.

Peer-reviewed studies on early 2024-2025 influenza season epidemiology in the United States provide case definitions, baseline activity context, and subtype distribution data that support correct interpretation of surveillance counts.

Reputable news outlets (e.g., AP, Reuters, STAT News) and situation reports (e.g., ProMED, HealthMap) may report on early influenza season activity in the United States during late September to early October 2024, providing supplementary signals and corroborating evidence quotes.
